description: Deterministic release-gate contract for the PetTripFinder Dayton market (PTF-PER-MARKET-RELEASE-CONTRACTS-001). Consumed by scripts/pettripfinder/assemble_netlify_bundle.py. Complete and self-contained: every number below is calibrated to THIS market's committed authority, and none of it is inherited from or comparable to Columbus's contract. Contains NO credentials and NO remote project identifiers. The committed hotel-policy package is the single identity authority for the verified hotels; this contract deliberately does NOT duplicate a hard-coded production allow-list.

deployment_authorization.means: A passing contract means this market's assembled package is STRUCTURALLY deployable: its authority files agree, its routes match its reviewed inventory, no held identity leaks, and every publish/tech gate holds. It is not a deployment authorization and it makes no claim that the market's identity universe is fully resolved -- 90 of this market's 129 confirmed identities are still unresolved.

identity_census.note: The census carries a per-record policy_state annotation from the field survey, and it marks eight properties VERIFIED_NO_PETS. That annotation is an observation, not authority: PTF-DAYTON-INTEGRATION-ADJUDICATION-001 adjudicated six of them into the committed exclusion registry and left two (Holiday Inn Express & Suites Troy, Hotel Versailles) unadjudicated, so they remain UNRESOLVED. The reconciliation below counts the registry's six, because the registry is what suppresses a route.

reconciliation.note: verified_no_pets counts ONLY VERIFIED_NO_PETS records this market owns in launch_packages/pettripfinder/hotel_exclusions.json. unresolved is UNKNOWN, never negative evidence: a failed capture answers nothing.

reconciliation_cross_checks.note: PTF-DAYTON-RECOVERY-WORKER-002 categorised every remaining unresolved identity into exactly two disjoint groups: candidates it proposes for promotion, and identities it could not resolve. Their combined length is this market's unresolved count, so a drift in either the contract or the derivation shows up here as a partition that no longer covers the total.

policy_package.note: The verified hotel identities are DERIVED from this package at assembly time via scripts.pettripfinder.site_data.verified_public_hotels(); they are not restated here. Held/manual-review hotels are this market's seed hotels absent from this package. The package is schema 1.0, not Columbus's 1.1 -- the version is a per-market fact, which is why the gate reads it from this contract rather than from a gate name.

public_surface.held_hotel_exclusion: Every seed hotel this market owns that is absent from the committed package (not-published seed hotels: held/manual-review plus rows still pending evidence) must have NO public route and NO reference on any surface: hotel profiles, the hotels listing/category page, nearby-lodging cards on any page, the policy-comparison table, the sitemap, canonicals, internal links, and /go/ interstitials. This market currently holds none -- every seed row it owns is published -- and the gate is derived, so it starts enforcing the moment that changes.

routes.note: route_mode market_prefixed: this market's hub, corridor, and policy-comparison pages live under /pet-friendly-hotels/dayton-oh/. Thirteen of its eighteen configured corridors are below their publication minimum and claim no route.

publish.note: The publish root must contain ONLY the static website plus the two Netlify control files. Build-internal reports the generator emits (_build_report.json, _broken_link_report.json, _quality_report.json, bundle_manifest.json) are read for gating but are excluded from site/ and must never ship.
